title: Under the world of AI-generated feedback on writing: mirroring motivation, foreign language peace of mind, trait emotional intelligence, and writing development
extended_summary:
This mixed-methods study examines whether AI-generated feedback on writing affects multiple outcomes in English as a Foreign Language (EFL) learners: writing proficiency, motivation, foreign language peace of mind (FLPoM), and trait emotional intelligence (EI). The paper is not focused on literacy subgroups or accessibility, but rather on whether AI feedback improves learners’ writing development and related affective variables.

The intervention compared two groups in a quasi-experimental design: an experimental group received online writing development with AI-generated feedback, while a control group completed the same online writing activities without AI-generated feedback. The study was conducted at the College of Languages, Nawroz University in Duhok, Kurdistan Region, Iraq, with 322 intermediate-level EFL learners aged 16–30. Quantitative instruments included pretest/posttest writing assessments and validated scales for FLPoM, trait EI, and motivation; qualitative semi-structured interviews were also conducted with 29 participants.

The quantitative results are internally inconsistent in the article’s narrative, but the inferential tables indicate significant posttest group effects for writing, FLPoM, EI, and motivation after controlling for pretest scores. The qualitative interviews similarly describe perceived gains in motivation, calmness, emotional regulation, and writing quality among students in the AI-feedback group. However, the study does not report subgroup analyses, differential effects for emergent readers, multilingual learners, students with disabilities, or any other accessibility-related subgroup. Claims about broader benefit are based on the overall sample rather than subgroup outcome data.

identified_tools.name: GenAI (General)
identified_tools.description: A general generative AI / LLM chatbot or feedback system used to generate writing feedback and support language learning, without a specific named product identified in the paper.
identified_tools.use_case: Used as AI-generated feedback during online EFL writing development; feedback was immediate, personalized, and addressed grammar, vocabulary, coherence, and structure.

findings.finding_summary: In this quasi-experimental mixed-methods study (n=322; EG=153, CG=169), AI-generated feedback improved writing performance on the posttest. The paper reports a statistically significant group effect in ANCOVA for writing (F=61.18, p=0.00, partial eta squared=.16), with the EG scoring higher than the CG on the writing posttest (EG M=58.05, CG M=48.88).
findings.measure: Writing posttest / writing proficiency rubric (coherence, grammar, vocabulary, structure)

findings.finding_summary: AI-generated feedback significantly improved Foreign Language Peace of Mind (FLPoM). The ANCOVA for FLPoM posttest showed a significant group effect (F=94.05, p=0.00, partial eta squared=.22), and the EG scored higher than the CG on the posttest (EG M=34.06, CG M=28.27).

The study reports a significant positive effect of AI-generated feedback on trait emotional intelligence (EI). For the EI posttest, the group effect was significant (F=15.26, p=0.00, partial eta squared=.04), and the EG mean was higher than the CG mean (EG M=99.13, CG M=92.19). The effect size was small.

Motivation improved significantly for learners receiving AI-generated feedback. The ANCOVA for motivation posttest reported a significant group effect (F=31.77, p=0.00, partial eta squared=.09), with the EG scoring higher than the CG (EG M=34.06, CG M=29.41).

quality_tier_rationale: This is a mixed-methods quasi-experimental study with a comparison group, but not a randomized trial. The evidence is still useful, though the design and the paper's limited reporting of subgroup analyses constrain causal certainty.
impact_tier_rationale: The writing outcome shows a medium effect (partial eta squared=.16), and FLPoM shows a larger effect (.22), while motivation is modest (.09) and EI is small (.04). Overall impact is best characterized as modest-to-medium, with the strongest effects on writing and FLPoM.
